## Terminal

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

You have one deck, and several audiences.
Some slides are for experts, and some slides are backups.
Without Veil, you show a slide and then skip it, or you keep one deck for each audience.

Veil lets you tag content with a group name.
During the talk, a key press shows or hides a group.
A hidden slide leaves the deck, so the slide numbers, the progress bar, and the overview stay correct.
The same tags work in HTML documents.
In other formats, Veil removes the hidden content when it renders.

## Quick start

Add the filter and the Reveal.js plugin to the front matter.
Then add the class `.veil` to the content to hide.

```markdown
---
format: revealjs
filters:
  - veil
revealjs-plugins:
  - veil
extensions:
  veil:
    groups:
      - name: expert
        shown: false
---

## Introduction

This slide is always shown.

## Proof {.veil group="expert"}

This slide is for experts.
```

Open the rendered deck and press `u`.
The popover shows a switch for the group `expert`, which is off.
Turn it on to bring the slide back.

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every option, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for each of them rendered.

## Where it works

Veil has a runtime for `html` and `revealjs`.
There, the reader shows and hides groups in the browser.
In all other formats, including `dashboard`, Veil removes the hidden content at render time.
The [Static formats](static-formats.qmd) page explains the details.
